# KyberNow

> KyberNow is free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) game and remote desktop streaming: install KyberNow Server on your computer, then play and work on it from all your devices, in a native app or in any web browser. It is a next-generation alternative to Sunshine + Moonlight, built on the Kyber streaming engine (by VLC developers) and the QUIC protocol. Currently in beta (0.x versions, not yet 1.0).

Key facts:

- **What it is**: self-hosted "your own cloud" streaming. Unlike cloud gaming services, nothing is rented and no third-party server sits between the computer and your devices. Reach it at home, or from afar through a VPN (Tailscale, WireGuard).
- **Latency**: 9.4 ms median from capture to display, measured on 19 October 2026 (RTX 3080 Ti at 3840 × 2160, 160 Hz, to a MacBook Pro M4 Max, local network, H.264).
- **Server**: Windows 10 or 11, any graphics card (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, eGPU) or the processor. One installer sets up the Kyber engine, a web console, a virtual display and virtual speakers per session, gamepad drivers and the firewall.
- **Clients**: your computer on all your devices. A web client served by the computer itself works on any computer, tablet or phone with a modern browser; native apps (today for Mac and Apple TV) decode the image in hardware for the lowest latency.
- **Versus Sunshine + Moonlight**: QUIC (RFC 9000) instead of GameStream; image always encrypted (TLS 1.3); a single port; virtual display at the device's resolution built in; pairing through Bonjour, QR code or an on-screen code instead of a PIN; Opus sound up to 7.1; browser client. Not yet: HDR.
- **Price**: free, no account, no subscription, no ads. Community, non-commercial project by Les Lignes Claires. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the Kyber team.
